title: I'm working on a tower defense game where you draft the enemies you fight!
author: greatcoltini
selftext:
Hey guys!

  
Wanted to share my current game progress and what I'm working on.

  
My game is called KingdomTD: Draft Your Demise - a game built with the Godot engine.

Before each wave, you select different enemies to face off against, with enemies having unique combos (i.e. Goblins swarm together), resistances (golems are resistant to arrows, bats dodge melee towers), and the harder the enemies to more gold you get!

  
I've been using Codex for development assistance, and several other AI services to help build the game.

1. Codex for most general use-cases, coding/planning/image generation (for 2d)
2. Codex builds sprites for me to create 3d models in Meshy
3. Meshy for creating the 3d models for the towers/enemies/etc.

  
If this looks interesting to you - please feel free to check out the Steam page here,

[Kingdom TD: Draft Your Demise on Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4990780/Kingdom_TD_Draft_Your_Demise/)



Originally, I had planned on using 2d sprites in a 3d world (some evidence of this still remains on my Steam page), but I since switched to using 3d models instead. I wasn't super happy with how the 2d in 3d look looked, and I think 3d models serve much better to make the visual aesthetics align. Curious to hear if other people have a lot of experience making 3d models and what tools you guys use.



In general, I would love to hear how others are using AI to assist their game dev workflows!

comments.author: greatcoltini
comments.body: Also, if people have good 3d model workflows and don't use meshy - I would be interested in what exactly you use (and it's cost)
